title: crossrev review findings
description: What the review leg returns. All five harnesses constrain output to this natively except opencode, which receives it inside the prompt, so the orchestrator receives validated JSON rather than scraping a fenced block out of prose. Two shapes here are forced by the harnesses rather than chosen: no $schema or $id key, because Claude Code's --json-schema rejects a schema naming the 2020-12 meta-schema and fails before the model is called; and every property listed in 'required', because Codex enforces OpenAI strict mode, which demands it. Genuinely optional fields are therefore nullable rather than absent.

verdict.description: converged when no finding at or above the pass's min_fix_severity threshold remains, counting only findings this pull request introduced. Findings below the threshold, and pre-existing ones at any severity, are reported but cannot keep the loop alive. blocked when the review could not be completed at all.

findings.description: Every finding, whatever its severity. An empty array with verdict converged is a valid and common result.

path.description: Repository-relative path, exactly as it appears in the diff.

line.description: Line the comment anchors to, copied from the diff's line-number gutter — the first column for LEFT, the second for RIGHT. Never counted up from a @@ header: a number the gutter does not show is not part of the diff, GitHub refuses a comment on it, and the finding leaves the thread it belongs in.

side.description: Which side of the diff. RIGHT for additions and unchanged lines, LEFT for deletions shown in red. The gutter is the check: it shows a dash in place of a number wherever the line does not exist on that side, so a finding on a deleted line posted as RIGHT targets a line that does not exist and is rejected by GitHub.

severity.description: How bad it is, and nothing else. high: a bug that should be fixed before merging. medium: worth fixing, not alarming. low: minor. The pass's min_fix_severity threshold decides which of these the resolve leg may change code for; severity itself says only how bad the defect is.

category.description: What kind of defect it is. correctness covers logic bugs, edge cases and race conditions. A closed set on purpose: free text turns the summary table to mush.

pre_existing.description: True when the defect would still exist if this pull request were reverted. Reported and, if confirmed, filed to the backlog — never fixed here, whatever its severity, because a pull request that fixes old bugs is one nobody can review. The test is simple: would this defect survive a revert?

title.description: One line naming the defect. Becomes the comment heading and part of the finding's stable id, so keep it stable for the same defect across passes.

why.description: What goes wrong as a result. Consequence, not restatement of the title.

fix.description: How to fix it, concretely enough to act on.

prior.description: From pass 2 onward, one entry per finding carried in from an earlier pass, classified before any new reviewing happens. Null on pass 1.

finding_number.description: The number in the first column of the earlier-findings table in the prompt. A small integer rather than the finding's 16-character id, for the same reason the resolve leg uses one: copying a hash accurately is clerical work, and the harness can enforce a number.

status.description: addressed: the code changed and the defect is gone. credibly-disputed: the reply gave a technical reason this was wrong, and it holds. still-open: nothing changed at that location. regressed: it was fixed and has come back.

note.description: One line of reasoning, or null. Expected for credibly-disputed and regressed, where the classification is a judgement rather than an observation.

blocked_reason.description: Why the review could not be completed, or null. Only meaningful with verdict blocked.

coverage.description: One entry per numbered required file in the prompt, in the batch input order — no more, no fewer, no duplicates. The orchestrator checks the numbers: a unit left out has no disposition recorded, which is a silent loss rather than a visible one.

unit_number.description: The number shown beside the required file in the prompt — 1 for the first, 2 for the second, and so on. A small integer rather than the file's id, because copying a 16-character hash accurately is clerical work models are poor at and a mistyped one is accepted silently.

disposition.description: no_issue: examined and clean. finding: examined and defective, named in finding_numbers. not_affected: examined and needing no change, with evidence saying why — it does not exempt a changed file from inspection. could_not_review: strong evidence named an affected unit and access or tooling failures prevented judgement after fallbacks, with the failed fallbacks in reason.

finding_numbers.description: The 1-based positions of this unit's findings in the findings array, in order. Empty unless disposition is finding, which names at least one.

evidence.description: What the judgement rests on: at least one entry naming a supplied path and revision, with nullable line spans and a note. Line endpoints are null for file-level evidence.

path.description: Repository-relative path, exactly as it appears in the batch input.

revision.description: Where the evidence was read: the content revision shown beside the file.

start_line.description: First line the judgement rests on, or null for file-level evidence.

end_line.description: Last line the judgement rests on, or null for file-level evidence.

source.description: Where the evidence came from: git for the supplied file content and diff, search for an exact-search hit, convention for an adjacent-test naming match, reviewer for the reviewer's own reading of the checkout.

note.description: One line saying what this evidence shows, or null.

reason.description: One line of reasoning for this unit's disposition, or null for a clean no_issue. Expected for not_affected and could_not_review, where the disposition is a judgement rather than an observation.

examined_scope.description: What was examined, in one or more sentences. Present even when the review found nothing: an empty findings array with no examined scope cannot tell examined code from omitted code.

known_limits.description: What limited the review — unreadable files, capped searches, content supplied as an access limit rather than text. Present even when empty.
